title: Kara C. Hoover
text:
Kara C. Hoover
  Biological Anthropologist & Data Scientist

  
    My experience bridges academic research to policy analysis and applied analytics. My domain expertise in anthropology is human biological and genetic variation and adaptation. My scientific research focuses on developmental instability & health disparity, olfactory science ecology & genetics, and climate health & adaptation. My applied projects focus primarily on social policy, international science, research landscape scoping, and forecasting. I specialize in translating complex data and research questions into actionable results through reproducible end-to-end workflows.

title: About Me
text:
I’m a biological anthropologist and data scientist with expertise spanning human biological variation, environmental health, and applied data analytics. My career bridges academic research, federal agencies, and industry, where I’ve led technical projects that integrate biological data, policy analysis, and computational methods to address complex questions in public health, international science policy, and social equity.
My academic research has examined human adaptation and variation across multiple biological systems – from developmental stress and climate adaptation to biomechanics of the skull and postcranial skeleton, genetic epidemiology of West Nile Virus, and the evolution and ecology of human olfaction. I’m particularly interested in how environmental change shapes human biology and creates health inequities, including Anthropocene-induced sensory inequities.
Throughout my career, I’ve applied data analytics to diverse questions, from population genetics and biomechanics to policy research and international science strategy. Over the past five years, my analytical focus has shifted toward natural language processing, network analysis, bibliometrics, and predictive modeling for policy applications. My recent work has centered on international science and technology policy, analyzing global R&D trends, research collaboration networks, and the relationship between democracy, education, and governance. I’ve developed interactive applications and analytical pipelines to evaluate program impact, forecast shifts in global research leadership, and examine connections between women’s empowerment and demographic outcomes.
My technical toolkit includes R, Python, and SQL for statistical analysis and modeling, with expertise in Bayesian methods, machine learning, geospatial analysis (QGIS, ArcGIS), phylogenetic analysis, text mining and NLP, network analysis, and interactive data visualization using Shiny and Quarto. I use GitHub for version control and collaborative development. I’m experienced in managing large datasets, building ETL pipelines, and developing reproducible analytical workflows that translate complex data into actionable intelligence and compelling visual narratives.
I thrive in collaborative, interdisciplinary environments and have experience mentoring students, coordinating multi-institutional research teams, and communicating complex findings to diverse audiences – from academic peers to policy stakeholders. Whether leading technical analyses, designing research strategies, or serving as a bridge between research and application, I’m driven by work that combines rigorous science with real-world impact.

title: Portfolio Website — Rules & Planning Document
text:
Site: https://kchoover14.github.io
Last updated: 2026-02-27



The portfolio is a Quarto website with four pages:

Landing page (index.qmd) — bio, skills cards, links
About Me (about.qmd) — full bio and publications list
Scientific Research (scientific-research.qmd) — eggplant theme, 8 project cards
Applied & Policy Research (applied-policy.qmd) — blues theme, 14 project cards




Navbar: About Me | Scientific Research | Applied & Policy Research | GitHub icon (right)
Site name/brand (“Kara C. Hoover”) in navbar links home — no separate Home tab
QMD source files are local-only and never committed to git. Only _site/ is pushed.





Make edits to QMD and SCSS files locally
Delete _site/ folder
Run quarto render
Push _site/ to GitHub
No YAML changes needed when swapping style-master.scss — filename stays the same








Blues (default / Applied & Policy pages) - Primary: #004080 - Used in: applied-policy.qmd - Body class: blues (default, no class needed)
Eggplant (Scientific Research / academic pages) - Primary: #6b3d72 - Primary dark: #532f5a - Used in: scientific-research.qmd and all individual project pages (smelling-in-the-wild, subsistence-impacts-occipital-biomechanics, peripheral-resilience-ryukyu-colonialism) - Body class: add body-classes: eggplant to QMD YAML
TOC active link color (eggplant pages): #45733E (forest green)
Landing page uses fern green (#6b8f71) — separate inline styles in index.qmd, not controlled by style-master.scss.



Each project repo needs its own style-master.scss (copy from portfolio root). No _quarto.yml changes needed — the SCSS filename is the same everywhere.







Every card must have exactly three pills: 1. DOI — links to the published article 2. Project page — links to the GitHub Pages portfolio page (https://kchoover14.github.io/repo-name/) 3. Repository — links to the GitHub repo (https://github.com/kchoover14/repo-name)
Cards without a project page yet still show the DOI and Repository pills. The Project page pill is added when the page is built. Cards already have a page but are missing DOI — this needs to be fixed (see Backlog).
Description rules: - Card description and GitHub repo description must match exactly — card is the master - For published projects: description is findings-forward (states the result, not just the question) - For unpublished or unreviewed projects: use a minimalist question-focused description (Ryukyu-style: describe the question/approach, not the finding) - For repos where scripts are being updated but no new analysis is being done: use the formula “Scripts and data for [publication title or topic].” — neutral, accurate, doesn’t overclaim - Journal name and year appear in italics at the end of the description for published work - Card and repo descriptions must mirror exactly — when in doubt, update the repo to match the card



Each card has two pills: 1. Project page — links to the GitHub Pages portfolio page 2. Repository — links to the GitHub repo
No DOI pills on blues cards (these are applied/data science projects, not journal publications).




DOI link: label is DOI
Portfolio page link: label is Portfolio page
GitHub repo link: label is GitHub repo

Add DOI pill to eggplant cards that have a project page — Subsistence/Occipital, Smelling in the Wild, Peripheral Resilience/Ryukyu currently show Portfolio page + Repository but are missing DOI. All three eggplant cards should have all three pills.
Build portfolio pages for: Hadza, Old Noses (OR Variation), Surveillance, Baboons — currently repo-only with DOI + Repository pills
Build portfolio page for Hunter-Gatherer Resilience (Kyushu)
New repo and card for COVID SES diagnosis-seeking paper (ses-symptom-variation-diagnosis) — description drafted, unpublished so question-forward
Add new repos as projects complete (e.g., ses-symptom-variation-diagnosis)
Set up daily local backup routine for QMD source files (lesson from git clean disaster — QMDs are local-only and not in git history)






Consider adding thumbnail images back to project cards (was removed earlier; revisit whether it improves visual appeal vs. clutter)

Location
Notes

Portfolio root (local only)
Landing page — 6 skill cards, bio, links


about.qmd
Portfolio root (local only)
Bio + publications list

Portfolio root (local only)
8 eggplant project cards


applied-policy.qmd
Portfolio root (local only)

_quarto.yml
Portfolio root
Site config and navbar — committed to git


style-master.scss
Portfolio root + each project repo
Master stylesheet — copy to each project repo


_site/
Portfolio root
Rendered output — only thing pushed to git








Never run git clean -fd — QMD source files are untracked by design and will be permanently deleted
Never run git reset --hard — same risk
Read-only diagnostics only: git status, git log, git diff
To force-stage a file Git thinks is unchanged: git add -f filename
Recovery of deleted untracked files: only possible from rendered HTML in _site/ — painful and imperfect
If Git pane shows phantom files (??): investigate with git status before taking any action
